title: PFD-15: n+2 source copies and linear quantum workspace

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). PFD-15 is the single algorithm in proof.md: m=n+2 clean copies, q_lab=n+ceil(log2 m)+10, q_G=ceil(m/2)+15, the specified coherent half-phase Grover filter, and total rotation-synthesis error at most 1/128. For n=1 it uses the exact three-copy branch. It returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 241/320>3/4. Total charged sequential work is O(2^(n/2) n^2 log2 n), including all acquisition, initialization, gate generation, addressing, measurements, precision and classical synthesis. The exact growth index of this envelope is 1. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every branch, including erroneous extracted labels and unsuccessful outputs. Constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The displayed representative applies for n>=2; n=1 has constant cost.

Exactly Q=n+2 original DCP source copies are acquired on every branch, including the finite branch. No verification or restart copies are used. Hence Q=O(n), with exact envelope growth index 0. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every branch, including erroneous extracted labels and unsuccessful outputs. Constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. With zero malformed copies, all acquired copies are independent ideal coset states and the same success and four resource bounds hold jointly. No positive malformed-copy tolerance or impossibility of such tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
